title: Yoke output is UTF-8 even when a harness captures it on Windows
when: A harness, pipe or test captures yoke, merge-engine or update-status output on native Windows, where Python writes pipes in the ANSI code page (cp1252).
need: Every yoke invocation, hooks included, switches stdout and stderr to UTF-8 before writing, so status arrows and non-ASCII paths never raise UnicodeEncodeError; the console code page itself is never changed. On Windows, CLI-launched Python modules start with UTF-8 for redirected stdout and stderr, including the merge-item child. A reader that closes the pipe early ends output quietly on every OS: Windows reports that write as EINVAL, POSIX as BrokenPipeError; other stream errors still fail.
surface: yoke CLI entry point and the engines it runs in-process or as children.
review: Native terminal capture drives the real entry point under cmd.exe, Windows PowerShell and pwsh with a cp1252-strict stdout; closed-pipe tests cover both OS error shapes. Windows suite runs own platform proof.
